title: ProcessRules
description: Data file content/processes/rules.json (B2537): heat levels in order and the basic processing rules. AI-found rules are added per world at runtime (job process) in the same form. When several rules match one try, the most specific wins: more inputs, then more required properties (properties_all over all inputs), then a tool condition, then a heat condition; ties by rule id (ordinal). The core (P3) applies exactly this order.

physics.description: Ground rules of physics for the judge of unknown tries (A1554, F5297 = A, B2616, D711): one place for all physics. The service checks every judgement against them and rules impossible tries out without a model call; the prompt reads the examples from here. Optional; absent = the prompt's own table (judge v1/v2).

heat_processes.description: Processes that work by heat (vocabulary process): they need heat in reach and a heat_min.

no_new.description: Properties a process gives only if an input already has them (never food or drink from nothing).

needs_any.description: Per process: some input must have one of these properties. Keys are process ids (checked against the vocabulary when the service starts).

never_if.description: Per process: no input may have any of these properties. Keys are process ids (checked against the vocabulary when the service starts).

may_add.description: Per process: the only properties it can give (a process not listed: no limit). Keys are process ids (checked against the vocabulary when the service starts).

may_remove.description: Per process: the only properties it can take away (not listed: no limit). Keys are process ids (checked against the vocabulary when the service starts).

examples.description: Short English sentences for the judge (internal, never shown to players; ADR-0007): tries that work and tries that do not. They show the strictness, not a list of answers.
